title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — I keep Art. 10; deny 'were devoted to death' in Adam's person (tense and wording)
pass_a_gloss: Placeus refuses the desertion charge—he holds the whole Confession, especially Art. 10—yet still denies 'were devoted to death in Adam's person.' He rejects Garrigues's wording: Placeus spoke present death, not past addiction; Paul's 'die / will be made alive' is not about a present devotion of that kind.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Do I desert that Confession, which I wholly embrace and tightly hold, especially that tenth article? Yet I deny that we were devoted to death in Adam's own person. First, those words "were devoted to death" are not mine: I did not use the past tense but the present, and I did not speak of devotion (addiction) but of death itself. For the Apostle's words run thus: in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive; they cannot be taken of a present devotion of that kind, as is clear from the future "will be made alive."
source_text: PLAC. Egone illam Confessionem desero, quam totam amplector, arcteque teneo, imprimis articulum illum decimum? At nego nos in ipsa Adami persona fuisse morti addictos. Primum illa verba, fuisse morti addictos, mea non sunt: neque praeterito usus sum, sed praesenti, neque de addictione locutus sum, sed de ipsa morte. Verba enim Apostoli sic aiunt: in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita & in Christo omnes vivificabuntur; de praesenti eiusmodi addictione intelligi non possunt, ut ex futuro, vivificabuntur, perspicuum est.

choices.choice: Keep Confession; reject past addictio; present death from Paul
